scope: Bounded native signal capability inspection for selected userScripts revocation fence, not new repository audit; no additional browser runs or author fixture changes

findings.claim: Both exact-tag public userScripts schemas expose functions but no toggle event, revocation history or monotonic authorization epoch. This is an API-surface finding; not proof that every possible native side channel is impossible.

The browser internally updates current allowed state, enables/disables dynamic source and sends SetUserScriptsAllowed IPC. Reviewed path does not emit a public extension revocation-history event. Internal IPC is not itself an exposed extension capability.

Renderer updates bindings, but GetAPIHelper returns a previously instantiated per-context cached API object. API object/function identity alone is not a revocation epoch. A claimed descriptor/binding side channel would require separate exact-version ordering, durability and genuine UI evidence; none is approved here.

Unchanged fixture accepts old native-completed result after genuine switch OFF then ON in both versions/worlds without test-injected recheck. This existing counterexample remains authoritative until corrected frozen candidate is provided.

pollingCounterexample.historyA: ON at t0; continuously ON; ON at t1
pollingCounterexample.historyB: ON at t0; OFF and ON entirely between native availability observations; ON at t1
pollingCounterexample.observation: Same successful current-state checks, same host/document, and no public durable history receipt. A poll-only observer cannot distinguish these histories.
pollingCounterexample.additionalSchedulingRisk: Timer interval is not maximum observation gap. Host event-loop pause, native response delay and browser process suspension can lengthen gaps; do not assume a minimum UI OFF dwell or instantaneous check-to-accept atomicity.
pollingCounterexample.consequence: Increasing poll rate, waiting for UI settling, or passing one long-OFF test cannot prove every transient revocation is fenced.

provableNarrowBoundary: When an operation-owned native availability check actually returns disabled/rejected, durably mark that operation and its earlier results invalid even after current authorization restores.
A genuine permissions.onRemoved observation can justify its documented host-permission fence; it cannot be assumed to represent the Allow User Scripts toggle.
An independently evidenced host/document incarnation change can invalidate old identities. Current UI cases did not observe natural host reconstruction.
Current checks can prove only authorization at the specific native check; they do not prove uninterrupted authorization since dispatch.
resolution: The approved unconditional real-revocation/old-result fence remains BLOCK. A narrower observed-revocation promise is descriptive only and cannot replace it without an explicit independently reviewed contract/capability amendment.
newFixReviewRequirements: Remove runner/reviewer calls that mutate operation fences. Measurement of UI/API state must remain read-only with respect to acceptance state.
Show operation-owned fail-closed invalidation and browser-backed event/incarnation/epoch with exact-version provenance and causal ordering before acceptance.

Real UI OFF→ON tests must cover native-pending and native-completed acceptance hold in both worlds and versions, restored-before-next-sample, delayed host task delivery, and later valid run. The counterexample need not add a full matrix solely for counts.

If using any binding/descriptors/Port/sentinel mechanism, demonstrate that every transition creates durable, authentic evidence even when transitions occur between host observations. Native internal update alone is insufficient.
Keep raw error-shape FAIL and wrapper-impact distinction, actual UI permission controls, old-document fencing and resource cleanup. No new privileges/backend or borrowed-tab closure.
Only frozen final two-lane union hash can receive overall F1 verdict; current round-5 plan approval is separate.
